options.text: The active transport of water against a gradient
The evaporation of water from leaves
The movement of any substance down its concentration gradient
The diffusion of water molecules through a partially permeable membrane from a dilute to a more concentrated solution

questions.explanation: Osmosis is the net movement of water molecules through a partially permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution).

questions.stem: What is a partially permeable membrane?

options.text: A membrane that allows all substances through
A membrane made of cellulose
A membrane that blocks everything
A membrane that allows some substances through but not others

questions.explanation: A partially (or selectively) permeable membrane contains tiny pores that allow small molecules like water to pass through but prevent larger molecules from passing.

questions.stem: What happens to an animal cell placed in pure water?

options.text: It becomes turgid
It swells and may burst (lyse)
Nothing happens
It shrinks

questions.explanation: An animal cell placed in pure water will absorb water by osmosis, swell, and may burst (lyse) because it has no cell wall to prevent over-expansion.

questions.stem: What prevents a plant cell from bursting when it absorbs water?

options.text: The nucleus
The cell wall
The cell membrane
The chloroplasts

questions.explanation: The rigid cellulose cell wall prevents the plant cell from bursting when water enters by osmosis. Instead, the cell becomes turgid as the wall resists further expansion.

options.text: When water moves into a cell
When cells divide by mitosis
When a plant cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall due to water loss
When an animal cell swells and bursts

questions.explanation: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell loses so much water that the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall. This happens when a plant cell is placed in a very concentrated solution.

questions.stem: In which direction does water move during osmosis?

options.text: From hot areas to cold areas
From high water potential to low water potential
It moves equally in both directions
From low water potential to high water potential

questions.explanation: Water always moves from a region of higher water potential (more dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (more concentrated solution) during osmosis.

questions.stem: A student places potato chips in different concentrations of salt solution. In which solution would the potato chip increase in mass?

options.text: Pure water
A concentrated salt solution
A solution with no water
A solution with the same concentration as the potato cells

questions.explanation: In pure water, water moves into the potato cells by osmosis because the water potential outside is higher than inside the cells. This causes the cells to swell and the potato chip to gain mass.
